image classification technology is important for the application of hyperspectral technology. Support vector machines (SVMs) work well in supervised classifications of hyperspectral images; however, they still have some shortcomings, and their use of a parallel decision plane makes it difficult to conform to real hyperspectral data distribution. The improved nonparallel support vector machine based on SVMs, i.e., the bias constraint additional empirical risk minimization nonparallel support vector machine (BC-AERM-NSVM), has improved classification accuracy compared its predecessor. However, BC-AERM-NSVMs have a more complicated solution problem than SVMs, and if the dataset is too large, the training speed is significantly reduced. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a least squares algorithm, i.e., the least square bias constraint additional empirical risk minimization nonparallel support vector machine (LS-BC-AERM-NSVM). The dual problem of the LS-BC-AERM-NSVM is an unconstrained convex quadratic programming problem, so its solution speed is greatly improved. Experiments on hyperspectral image data demonstrate that the LS-BC-AERM-NSVM displays a vast improvement in terms of solution speed compared with the BC-AERM-NSVM and achieves good classification la minimisation du risque empirique<\/jats:title>\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\"fr\">Dans ce manuscrit, nous pr\u00e9sentons et \u00e9tudions des strat\u00e9gies d\u2019\u00e9chantillonnage appliqu\u00e9es, \u00e0 probl\u00e8mes li\u00e9s \u00e0 l\u2019apprentissage statistique. L\u2019objectif est de traiter les probl\u00e8mes qui surviennent g\u00e9n\u00e9ralement dans un contexte de donn\u00e9es volumineuses lorsque le nombre d\u2019observations et leur dimensionnalit\u00e9 contraignent le processus d\u2019apprentissage. Nous proposons donc d\u2019aborder ce probl\u00e8me en utilisant deux strat\u00e9gies d\u2019\u00e9chantillonnage: - Acc\u00e9l\u00e9rer le processus d\u2019apprentissage en \u00e9chantillonnant les observations les plus utiles. - Simplifier le probl\u00e8me en \u00e9cartant certaines observations pour r\u00e9duire la complexit\u00e9 et la taille du probl\u00e8me. Standard classification models optimizing cross-entropy loss provide uncalibrated softmax posteriors that do not reflect predictive unfamiliarity. In this paper, we establish an empirical, reproducible benchmarking framework investigating model reliability across four foundational pillars: (i) confidence calibration via validation-tuned Temperature Scaling, (ii) predictive uncertainty quantification via Deep Ensembles (M=3), (iii) out-of-distribution (OOD) detection across four complementary score formulations (Maximum Softmax Probability, Predictive Entropy, Logit-Based Free Energy, and Penultimate Feature-Space Mahalanobis Distance), and (iv) distribution-free finite-sample guarantees through Split-Conformal Prediction and Selective Risk-Coverage Abstention. Evaluating on standardized biomedical datasets spanning colorectal histology (PathMNIST, N=107,180), microscopic hematology cytology (BloodMNIST, N=17,092), and pediatric chest radiographs (PneumoniaMNIST, N=5,856), we uncover critical structural failure modes in conventional output-space scoring. Specifically, Maximum Softmax Probability and Free Energy collapse on far-OOD radiographic images (AUROC &lt; 17%) due to background feature activation, whereas penultimate feature Mahalanobis distance achieves near-perfect separation (99.99% AUROC on far-OOD radiographs and 96.96% AUROC with 0.04% FPR95 on near-OOD blood cytology). Deep ensembles enhance near-OOD uncertainty estimation (+13.17% AUROC over single networks), and temperature scaling reduces Expected Calibration Error from 7.37% to 6.48% while preserving OOD rank order. Split-conformal prediction provides valid 90.41% empirical coverage with an average prediction set size of 1.54 classes, while selective prediction boosts accuracy from 81.55% to 88.26% by abstaining on the 20% most uncertain inputs.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7598822","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Reliable Medical Image Classification Through Out-of-Distribution Detection, Uncertainty Quantification, and Conformal Prediction: A Benchmark on MedMNIST"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0004-7111-7326","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Paras","family":"Rajput","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7598822"},{"DOI":"10.1134\/s105466181003003x","title":["Exact combinatorial bounds on the probability of overfitting for empirical risk minimization"],"author":[{"given":"K. Cette classification fait appel en g\u00e9n\u00e9ral \u00e0 des m\u00e9thodes d'apprentissage et \u00e0 des classifieurs qui doivent r\u00e9pondre \u00e0 la fois \u00e0 la pr\u00e9cision ainsi qu'\u00e0 la rapidit\u00e9. Ces probl\u00e8mes d'apprentissage touchent aujourd'hui un grand nombre de domaines d'applications: \u00e0 savoir, le web (profiling, ciblage, r\u00e9seaux sociaux, moteurs de recherche), les \"Big Data\" et bien \u00e9videmment la vision par ordinateur tel que la reconnaissance d'objets et la classification des images. La pr\u00e9sente th\u00e8se se situe dans cette derni\u00e8re cat\u00e9gorie et pr\u00e9sente des algorithmes d'apprentissage supervis\u00e9 bas\u00e9s sur la minimisation de fonctions de perte (erreur) dites \"calibr\u00e9es\" pour deux types de classifieurs: k-Plus Proches voisins (kNN) et classifieurs lin\u00e9aires. Ces m\u00e9thodes d'apprentissage ont \u00e9t\u00e9 test\u00e9es sur de grandes bases d'images et appliqu\u00e9es par la suite \u00e0 des images biom\u00e9dicales. Ainsi, cette th\u00e8se reformule dans une premi\u00e8re \u00e9tape un algorithme de Boosting des kNN et pr\u00e9sente ensuite une deuxi\u00e8me m\u00e9thode d'apprentissage de ces classifieurs NN mais avec une approche de descente de Newton pour une convergence plus rapide.
